limitations_and_boundaries: TiMINo causality may output 'I do not know' when model assumptions are violated, but this can also lead to wrong conclusions on small datasets due to the null hypothesis representing independence.
The method can be computationally intractable for time series with many components if feedback loops are present.
For large sample sizes, even smallest differences between the true data generating process and the model may lead to rejected independence tests.
The algorithm does not yet test for non-vanishing autocorrelations in the residuals.
The method may fit a model only in the wrong direction, requiring unnatural fine-tuning of functions, relevant only when time series lack time structure or data are non-faithful.
The Bonferroni correction in HSIC-based independence test may require modifications for a high number of time series components.

methods.name: TiMINo causality algorithm
methods.protocol_description: Algorithm 1: For time series without feedback loops, iteratively fit TiMINo for each component using past values and contemporaneous values of other components, test independence of residuals, select the component with weakest dependence, and remove non-required parents. If no model with independent residuals is found, output 'I do not know'.
